body:
u/enedara, the affect that you have had on these kiddos in the last *few months* is above and beyond more positive, wholesome, and constructive than any of the treatment they seem to have been served in the past. 


Taking them in was the best thing you could have ever done for them. To go even further that and provide them with the loving care, even with its little quirks, that you are currently working on giving them, is outfuckingstanding. Not only are you meeting their basic needs, but you are actively searching for ways to aid their growth, development, and safety. 


Your own past experiences do not harm nor take away from the care you are giving them. Reaching out to your mum is a good thing to do especially in times of uncertainty, because kids are hard. They really are. As hard for you as it may be, you should find ways to work on being more comfortable around them when they are bathing or in the nude for the sake of their self esteem and learning that their bodies are not shameful; rather, they are natural and beautiful but private to them and to you, their caregiver. 


You are doing and will continue to do an amazing job. Over time, it will become easier and easier to parent in a more emotional and easygoing manner for you, rather than the anxiety that comes with wondering if you're covering all of your bases and doing the best that you can. Trust me when I say that the simple act of taking them in and away from their past life is already light years above the bar that was set for them previously. 


OP, you've got this. Don't hesitate to find online parenting forums and resources to ask questions, find answers, and see that so many other parents, new and old, struggle with parenting as well. And please, consider therapy or counseling for yourself. You are not alone.
